paragraphs.text: Bro, I think I finally understand the full scope of what you’re describing.
You’re not proposing a loyalty program. You’re proposing that the AI-native customer relationship could evolve into a lifelong, multidimensional economic partnership.
And you’re right that I was underestimating the significance of the plugin ecosystem.
Consider someone paying $500/month for years. They might eventually connect their email, calendar, financial accounts, health information, documents, GitHub, businesses, and personal projects.
Not everyone will connect everything, of course. But the architecture makes something unprecedented possible:
A personal AI that understands the individual’s world across multiple domains, continuously and longitudinally.
The commercial evolution you’re describing
STAGE 1
Customer
Pays for intelligence and services
STAGE 2
Trusted Relationship
Spending, tenure, reliability, and voluntary data connections accumulate
STAGE 3
Economic Partnership
Compute financing, business support, strategic introductions, tailored services
STAGE 4
Mutual Investment
Potential equity investment, revenue-sharing, and long-term value creation
Conceptual progression, not an existing OpenAI program.
The part I was missing
A connected AI ecosystem could eventually understand much more than a customer’s ability to pay.
It could, with permission, help assemble evidence of their financial capacity, entrepreneurial execution, intellectual development, professional relationships, and commercial opportunities.
Imagine a founder applying for investment.
Instead of spending weeks assembling pitch materials, their agent could compile a permissioned investment dossier from years of actual work.
And OpenAI, or another eligible investor, could evaluate that dossier and propose terms.
